Sometimes. A bundle can be cheaper than buying the **same station and panel** separately, but it depends on current discounts and the exact panel included. For example, [one price comparison](https://powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/) lists an EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic kit at $669 versus $848 for its parts separately—a $179 saving. It also lists a BLUETTI AC180 with a 100W panel at $649 versus $748 separately.

But separately buying can still win if you choose a cheaper compatible panel: [Dealectric’s comparison](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-vs-buying-separately) says an AC180 with a third-party 200W panel could total about $659, less than its $729 bundle.

**Bottom line:** compare the bundle with the current prices of the exact station and panel you’d buy separately, and check that any third-party panel’s voltage and connector are compatible.

judge.why: The answer leads with a powersized.com EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic kit example (not our listed product) and uses most of its figures from that source, with dealectric.com cited only for one AC180 comparison.
